✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Twist with type conversion on the classical string palindrome problem

Binary output issue
* According to the contribution guidelines, binary outputs should be avoided for clashes. That's exactly the issue with your clash, as it allows only two possible answers (either "YES" or "NO"). Please modify the output requirement to allow for more than two possible answers, e.g. output the palindrome when [[N]] is a mirror number or "NO" when it is not.

Formatting / presentation
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly as described in the points below.

Goal
* Please format "N" as a [[variable]].

Input
* Please format "N" as a [[variable]].

Output
* Please format "N" as a [[variable]].

* Please format "YES" and "NO" as {{constants}}.

Constraints
* Please add this as a constraint:
1 ≤ [[N]] ≤ 99

Game modes
* It's almost impossible to guess the task in Reverse mode. Consider disabling that mode.

Cases
* Each test and its validator should cover the same scenario but with slightly different inputs (and outputs where applicable). Please revise all validators accordingly.

* Please add Test 9 and Validator 9 to cover the scenario of [[N]] being a single-digit number.

* Please add Test 10 and Validator 10 to cover the scenario of [[N]] being a multiple of 10.

Title
* Consider removing "Problem:" from the title.

Thanks.
Thank you for fixing the binary output issue. Please follow up the remaining issues.
I have changed everything to meet the requirements. Thank you for your incredibly helpful suggestions.

Thank you for following up. There are still some outstanding matters:

Title
* Consider removing "Problem:" from the title.

Output
* Please format the output phrases as {{constants}} like this:

{{Yes, [[N]] is a Mirror Number}}
{{No, [[N]] is a Palindrome}}
{{No, [[M]] is not a Palindrome}}

Cases
* Each test and its validator should cover the same scenario but with slightly different inputs and outputs. Please revise all validators accordingly. For example, you may change the input of Validator 1 to 65. Validators 2 to 10 should be revised similarly.

Thanks again.

I think there may be a misunderstanding. I did not mean that 56 should be used as the input for all validators 😅

My request is that each test and its validator should cover the same scenario, but the validator should use different input and output values from the test.

For example:

Test 1 and Validator 1 both cover a 2-digit mirror number. Test 1 uses 56. So, Validator 1 could use 65 instead.

Test 2 and Validator 2 both cover a 2-digit number which is not a palindrome. Test 2 uses 87. So, Validator 2 could use 86 instead.

So, for each test/validator pair, focus on the type of number being tested. Then think of a different number of that type and use it in the validator.

Please revise Validators 1 to 10 in that way.

Hope this is clearer. Just ask if you do not know what to do.

Thank you for the clarification. I understand the requirement now.

I have revised Validators 1–10 so that each validator covers the same scenario as its corresponding test case, but uses different input and output values.

Thank you for explaining the intended approach.

I don't see any changes yet. Maybe the contribution was not saved?

Also, would you please add "write answer" in Line 2 of the stub generator?

Thanks.
I have updated the stub generator as requested by adding “write answer” in Line 2. Thank you for the suggestion, I have also double-checked the change.

OK, this is looking better. The cases still need some adjustments.

* Test 1 is 56 + 65 = 121 (3-digit). Shall we use 65 for Validator 1? 13 is not a good choice because we already have Test 2 and Validator 2.

* Please change Test 3 to use another number that is not a palindrome, so that it is similar to Validator 3.

* Please change Validator 5 to use another multiple of 11, so that it is similar to Test 5.

* Please change Validator 6 to use another 1-digit number, so that it is similar to Test 6.

* Please add Test 8 and Validator 8 to use 3-digit palindromes such as 202 and another number.

* Please add Test 9 and Validator 9 to use 3-digit numbers that are not palindromes, such as 119 and another number.

Thanks.

Thank you for the detailed feedback.

I have updated the test cases according to your suggestions

Thank you again for the review. If you notice anything else that should be adjusted or if additional test coverage would be helpful, please feel free to suggest it.

We're almost there!

Cases
* Validator 5: Please use a 2-digit multiple of 11.

* Validator 9: Please use a 3-digit [[N]] that makes a 4-digit [[M]] that is not a palindrome, e.g. 951.

* Please add Test 10 and Validator 10: a 3-digit [[N]] mirror number that makes a 4-digit palindrome. For example, you may use 704 and 803.

Thanks.

Thank you for the additional review.

I have made the requested updates:

Validator 5 has been changed to use a 2-digit multiple of 11.
Validator 9 has been updated to use a 3-digit [[N]] that produces a 4-digit [[M]] which is not a palindrome (following the example of 951).
Added Test 10 and Validator 10 using 3-digit mirror numbers that produce a 4-digit palindrome, similar to the examples 704 and 803.

Thank you for your continued feedback. If there are any remaining adjustments or additional edge cases that should be covered, please let me know and I will update them accordingly.
Test 10 and Validator 10 should use a 3-digit **mirror number** that produce a 4-digit **palindrome**. 179 and 899 are not mirror numbers.
Thank you for your feedback. I have reviewed the requirements and will adjust Test 10 and Validator 10 to meet the criteria.
Thank you. It looks ok now.
Thank you for your feedback which helped improve my contribution.
